summary: This program stores seven facts about a giraffe in variables, using the three most common Python data types — text (str), decimal numbers (float), and whole numbers (int), plus a True/False value (bool) — and then prints them all as a formatted list.

lines.text: Text wrapped in quotation marks is a string, Python's data type for words and names.
A number written with a decimal point is a float, which is the right choice for a measurement that is not a whole number. Including the unit in the variable name keeps the meaning clear.
A number with no decimal point is an integer, suitable here because the weight is being recorded as a round figure.
Counted things are always integers, since you cannot have half a spot.
A boolean holds only True or False. Naming such a variable as a yes/no question, with an is_ prefix, makes it read naturally wherever it is used.

The f before the quotation mark makes this an f-string, so each name inside curly braces is replaced by that variable's value. Python converts the float, integers, and boolean to text automatically, and each \n starts a new line, so one print call produces seven lines of output.
